# Glossary — Hormozi's Coined Terms

The engine uses these terms verbatim. One-line definitions; full method lives in the linked reference.

## $100M Offers

- **Grand Slam Offer** — an offer so good people feel stupid saying no; differentiated and *incomparable*
  to competitors, so the buyer makes a value-based (not price-based) decision. (`offer-creation-5-step.md`)
- **Value Equation** — the formula for perceived value: **(Dream Outcome × Perceived Likelihood of
  Achievement) ÷ (Time Delay × Effort & Sacrifice)**. Increase the top two, decrease the bottom two.
  (`value-equation.md`)
- **Dream Outcome** — what the customer actually wants to *experience* (the vacation, not the plane
  flight). "Sell the destination."
- **Perceived Likelihood of Achievement** — the customer's belief it will work *for them specifically*.
- **Time Delay** — how long between purchase and outcome. Decrease it. "Fast beats free."
- **Effort & Sacrifice** — what the customer must do/give up. Decrease it toward zero.
- **Starving Crowd** — the market. Levers of success in order: **Starving Crowd (market) > Offer
  Strength > Persuasion Skills.** (`market-selection.md`)
- **The 4 market indicators** — Massive Pain · Purchasing Power · Easy to Target · Growing.
- **Convergent vs Divergent Thinking** — offers are built with *divergent* thinking (many solutions to
  one problem), not convergent (one right answer).
- **The Brick Exercise** — the 120-second divergent-thinking warm-up (list every use of a brick).
- **Sales-to-Fulfillment Continuum** — the trade-off between easy-to-sell and easy-to-fulfill.
  Mantra: **"Create flow. Monetize flow. Then add friction."**
- **Product Delivery Cheat Codes** — the dimensions to vary a solution: personal attention
  (1:1 / group / one-to-many); effort (DIY / DWY / DFY); medium; consumption format; speed; the 10x/¹⁄₁₀ test.
- **Trim & Stack** — remove high-cost/low-value items, keep low-cost/high-value + high-cost/high-value,
  then stack the survivors into the **Final High Value Deliverable**.
- **Scarcity / Urgency / Bonuses / Guarantees / Naming** — the five offer enhancers.
  (`offer-enhancers.md`, `guarantee-taxonomy.md`, `magic-naming.md`)
- **M-A-G-I-C** — the naming formula: **M**agnetic reason why · **A**vatar · **G**oal · time **I**nterval
  · **C**ontainer word.
- **The virtuous cycle of price** — charging more funds better delivery, which raises value, which
  justifies charging more. (`pricing.md`)

## $100M Leads

- **Lead** — a person you can contact. An **engaged lead** (someone who showed interest) is the true
  output of advertising.
- **Lead Magnet** — a complete solution to a narrow problem, given free to get engaged leads; the
  7-step process builds it. (`lead-magnet-7-step.md`)
- **The Core Four** — the only four ways to get leads: **Warm Outreach · Post Free Content · Cold
  Outreach · Paid Ads.** (`core-four.md`)
- **Rule of 100** — advertise to 100 people/day (reach out to 100, post content, or spend on ads)
  every day for 100 days.
- **Content Unit (Hook · Retain · Reward)** — the structure of any piece of content.
- **Client-Financed Acquisition (CFA)** — get enough cash from a new customer fast enough that
  acquiring them pays for itself, so you can outspend everyone.
- **Lead Getters** — get *other people* to advertise for you: **Customers (referrals) · Employees ·
  Agencies · Affiliates & Partners.** All about *leverage*. (`lead-getters.md`)
- **More / Better / New** — how to scale the Core Four: do more, do it better, or add a new method.
- **Open To Goal** — keep advertising each day until you hit your lead/sales goal, not until you've
  done a fixed amount. The Rule of 100 "on steroids."
